subject: Snapshot sanitization chain-of-custody — evidence request
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@clearfield.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: audit-team@clearfield.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Snapshot sanitization evidence request for SOC2 audit

Hi Karthik,

We're working through the ClearField SOC 2 evidence collection and have a focused ask around tenant snapshot handling. The auditors want: a) a clear description of the automated snapshot sanitization process; b) chain-of-custody artifacts that show when snapshots were created and sanitized; and c) a cryptographic hash listing or equivalent to demonstrate the sanitization run was executed for the production tenants in scope (prod-*/us-west-2). Ideally this is scoped to the May 2026 snapshot window.

Can Redwood provide:
- The ops runbook or playbook used for snapshot sanitization (versioned).
- A CSV of snapshot IDs with creation timestamps and sanitization timestamps + hashes (or signed attestation).
- A short note explaining how retained backups are prevented from containing PII after sanitization (high level is fine).

Auditor timeline: they need the artifacts for review by next Tuesday (2026-05-26). If we can get a packet or interim artifacts earlier that would be helpful.

Thanks — really appreciate a single point of contact for follow-ups.

Best,
Marta
Senior IT Audit Manager
ClearField Financial
[Attachment: clearfield-evidence-scope.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

Folks — looping you in to pull artifacts and confirm scope.

Marta: thanks for the clear ask. Internal plan below (will share artifacts once Monica confirms):

Action items:
- Monica: pull the May snapshot run logs for prod-* (us-west-2), export snapshot IDs, created_at, sanitized_at, and the hash outputs. Please attach the CSV and a brief explanation of the hashing process.
- Neha: provide the versioned ops runbook for sanitization and a 2–3 bullet high-level description of how we ensure PII is removed from snapshots and what controls prevent retention (truncate/zero, script-driven removal, verification).
- Jonas: confirm whether any archival systems retained pre-sanitized blobs during the process window and whether those were swept; if yes, include timestamps and disposition.

Timeline: Monica & Neha — can we aim to have a draft packet by Monday EOD (2026-05-25)? That gives Marta and the auditors a day to triage before the Tuesday deadline. If there are blockers, call them out now.

Thanks — Karthik

On Fri, May 22, 2026 at 10:05 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Folks — looping you in to pull artifacts and confirm scope.
> 
> Action items:
> - Monica: pull the May snapshot run logs for prod-* (us-west-2), export snapshot IDs, created_at, sanitized_at, and the hash outputs. Please attach the CSV and a brief explanation of the hashing process.
> - Neha: provide the versioned ops runbook for sanitization and a 2–3 bullet high-level description of how we ensure PII is removed from snapshots and what controls prevent retention (truncate/zero, script-driven removal, verification).

Thanks — all done. Attached are the two items requested: the ops runbook (sanitization-ops-runbook.pdf) and a snapshot CSV (snapshot-hashlist.csv). Highlights:

- Runbook: describes the automated pipeline (sanitizer v2.3), the cron window used for May 2026, rollback and verification steps, and the operator sign-off flow. It includes the script hash (sha256) and runbook version tag.
- CSV snapshot-hashlist.csv: sample rows include snapshot_id, created_at, sanitized_at, sanitizer_version, sha256_after_sanitize. Only production tenants in scope are included (prod-45, prod-72, prod-96). Hashes are produced by the sanitization pipeline immediately post-run.

A couple of clarifications for the auditors:
- The sanitizer is deterministic and removes PII-bearing columns based on the tenant schema mapping in the runbook. Verification is by checksum delta and a content-sampling step (see runbook §4).
- We do not retain pre-sanitized snapshot blobs in long-term archival storage. Temporary pre-sanitized copies live on the sanitizer worker for up to 24 hours and are deleted as part of the run closure; we capture deletion events in the job logs (included).

Attachments: [sanitization-ops-runbook.pdf (PDF, 340KB)], [snapshot-hashlist.csv (CSV, 26KB)]

Let me know if the auditors need signed attestations; we can produce a signed CSV export and provide a short attestation letter.

—Monica
Product Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@clearfield.com>

- Can Redwood produce a signed attestation for the CSV (sha256 of the CSV + a PGP-signed note) so auditors can validate ingestion integrity?
- We need one short paragraph from Product Security (Karthik) confirming the policy that pre-sanitized temporary copies are deleted within 24 hours and that retention policies block archival of pre-sanitized blobs.

If you can provide those two items by Monday morning (2026-05-25 12:00 PM PDT) the audit will be able to close this line item.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Marta

ClearField Financial
